OCTOBER EMPLOYEE OF THE MONTH: @anthony_ruggiero 

Ant has been with us for over a year now (shoutout Aunt Mare) and we couldn’t be happier. We do our best to provide an atmosphere where it is easy for everyone who comes in to leave their problems at the door, and nobody does a better job of that than Ant. This is an always happy, high energy, full of life guy who genuinely cares about the well being of everyone around him.

Loved by all staff and customers, Ant has been an amazing addition to the team. The only guy who would trek to spirit Halloween and wait in line for an hour to get a costume for a day where nobody else wore a costume. The only guy to stay hours after he clocked out to make sure the bar was cleaner for the morning staff. His value is undeniable and deserves recognition this month. Come pay him a visit all weekend long!

SEPTEMBER EMPLOYEE OF THE MONTH: @madisonroselucas 

Madison exemplifies what it means to work at Green Rock. If you’ve been in over the course of the last few months, Madison is likely the first face you’ve seen when you walk through the door - and that is fully intentional. 

She radiates positive energy to the staff & customers, is always dancing & smiling, and consistently putting the business first. After long weeks of teaching middle school & coaching high school varsity volleyball - she leaves everything at the door to show all those who come in a great time.

caption:
DO YOU KNOW DAVE?!

Another wonderful Thanksgiving Dinner is in the books! This year, The Madison Bar & Grill once again teamed up with the HCC to host a warm and welcoming celebration for residents of our HCC Affordable Housing Program. It’s a tradition that continues to remind us how powerful it is when a community comes together.

This special evening was made even more meaningful thanks to the participation and support of our HCC Board and HCC Pantry Senior Leadership Team members, who joined residents in sharing this annual tradition.

We’re especially grateful to Dave Carney, whose generosity and steady support make this event possible year after year. Your heart for our mission shines through in everything you do.

Huge thanks as well to the talented kitchen and wait staff for preparing a delicious meal and creating such a special evening for our residents.

@david.carney @_madisonbarandgrill

Just when we thought the hardest part was over, Zahra reminded us she’s a master escape artist.

After her spay, she Houdini’d her way out of a surgical onesie and went after her sutures — which sent us to urgent care and onto antibiotics. That was the moment we decided… Christmas came early.

A sweater over the onesie did what nothing else could. She accepted her fate. No escapes. No tricks.

This wasn’t a day or a week — this was the month we had to adapt.

And she did. 🤍

Part 5 is where everything opens up 🐾

Meet Skyler 💔🐾
Skyler has been waiting 14 whole months at the Associated Humane Society of Newark (Newark, NJ). That’s a long time to be overlooked, especially when you’re as wonderful as she is.
She’s a 5-year-old, 60-lb sweetheart—loving, affectionate, house-trained, and full of life. The kind of dog who just wants to be with her people and finally feel safe. 🥺
Here’s the important stuff:
🐶 Dog selective, but she has potential with bigger dogs, pending a proper meet
👧 Ok’d for big kids
💕 Thrives with love, structure, and patience
Skyler was heartbreakingly adopted and returned twice by the same family at no fault of her own, and shelter life is really wearing her down. This will be her second Christmas in a kennel… and no dog deserves that. 💔🎄

It’s not just about choosing between lunch options or what to wear. Sometimes decision paralysis runs deep👇🏻

It can be tied to the fear of upsetting others, feeling responsible for their moods, or not being “perfect” enough.

When you grow up trying to manage everyone else’s feelings, it’s easy to lose sight of your own. 

The need to keep the peace, avoid conflict, and make everyone happy becomes deeply ingrained. 

And now, as an adult, you’re facing decisions that force you to prioritize your own needs and it can feel extremely paralyzing and frustrating.

So, why does decision paralysis happen? When you’ve been conditioned to keep everyone else happy, the idea of disappointing someone feels like a huge risk. 

You might fear rejection, conflict, or the idea that you’re being selfish by choosing your own needs.

 It’s a heavy burden to carry, and it leaves you stuck, overthinking, and second-guessing every choice you make.

But what if we flipped the script? What if choosing what’s right for you didn’t have to come with guilt?

Remind yourself:

✨You are allowed to make decisions that prioritize your own needs, even if it means disappointing someone else. It doesn’t make you a bad person or selfish—it makes you human. When you start respecting your own feelings, you teach others to do the same.

Happy Sunday everyone! Matt was a big world traveler this weekend (dts) so we do not have a new lunch series review but good news: we tried a new sushi place this week! We’re just gonna apologize in advance for the photo quality, it was very dark inside (& we’re not advanced enough for flash photos) 😁🤳🏼 We have walked past Sushi Lounge hundreds of times (on our way to Jersey Mikes) and finally went in this week 🍣🍱

Sushi Lounge:
- Rating: 8/10 (Liz) 8/10 (Matt)
- Price Range: $$ ($50-$100)
- For appetizers, we tried the boneless spare rib lettuce wraps and they were delicious, a little hard to manage, but really flavorful
- Liz also got a classic spicy tuna roll for an appetizer and she claims it may be the most fresh sushi she’s had in Hoboken. When we come back, shes only getting sushi because of how good it was 🤤
- For entrees, Matt got the chicken hibachi and Liz got the tofu teriyaki (very random! we know!). Matt says the hibachi was good but he didn’t like that they didn’t prepare everything on his plate hibachi style - only the chicken. Liz enjoyed the tofu teriyaki but really thought the best menu item was the sushi!
- We made the reservation the day of and they still had a bunch but there were also a ton of people there

As a vegetarian, I was thrilled to discover their extensive menu, which offers plenty of delicious options.
During my visit, I indulged in the vegetable sushi roll, edamame, and their must-try Asian guacamole, which was a delightful surprise. I also enjoyed the miso soup and house salad—everything was fresh and flavorful. What impressed me the most was their commitment to customizing dishes according to dietary preferences. For instance, I was able to enjoy hibachi rice without any fish sauce, meat, or egg, and the vegetable yaki udon was simply delicious.
The attentive staff made sure I had exactly what I wanted, enhancing my dining experience. Whether you’re a sushi lover or looking for great vegetarian options, I highly recommend Sushi Lounge in Hoboken—it’s a place worth visiting!

Their $25 IT Girl Dinner (pasta, truffle fries, Caesar salad + a cocktail) is such a deal and the portions were big enough for leftovers. You can pick from three cocktails (Espresso Martini, Vodka Martini, or Femme Fatale). We chose Femme Fatale and it slapped.
Note: Our “spicy” cavatappi had zero spice 😒 definitely needed more flavor.

We also hit their Happy Hour 3-5 PM daily, bar area only, where everything is $10. We tried the pepperoni flatbread, buffalo wings, margarita, cheesesteak eggrolls. we also tried their holiday drink. Wings were juicy, eggrolls were fire, flatbread solid, and that margarita was strong strong.

Truffle fries? So good.
Caesar salad? Classic.
Still a cute happy hour moment

Okay! I decided to bring my @beli_eats reviews over to Shelby’s snack. I honestly think I wasn’t getting the credit I deserved over there (for worry I’ll be posting reviews in both places now) 

Let’s get into it! So we have been talking about wanting to try @antique_bar_bakery  for a while, like before I moved while. Well a few weeks ago I saw they had a prime 7:15 table for 2 on Burger Club Thursday available…. HADDDD to snag that! 

We go…i was soooo excited all day kept stalking their insta to see what the burger of the week was, telling my friends and debating the bread pudding or not. The whole 9 yards.

The burger was a breakfast style burger, had fried onion, egg, & fried picatta and the burger itself was a rib-eye patty. They also offered it as a combo w a glass of wine or a beer! & obvi it came w fries! 

So we got that, along with their normal burger, they say it’s rated in the top 15 burgers in NYC…interesting because we are in New Jersey but I’m not asking questions! It’s a thick patty, with LTO, cheese, pickles (that tasted homemade 😋) with a special sauce, IMO the sauce was a little on the spicy side for me.

We split both burgers- no apps bc we knew we wanted the bread pudding.

We both loved the burger club burger, i thought their classic burger was good, not my fav (I didn’t care for the sauce) !! The thing about Burger club is, the burgers are never repeated so it’s a one and done situation.

Now let’s get into the Star ⭐️ of the show 🔦 The bread pudding…. Okay come on… ITS HUGE!!!!!!!! It serves 4 (they are selling themselves short- it could serve 5 or 6!) it’s topped with powdered sugar & a table side warm caramel sauce poured ontop🤌🏻 it was FINEEEEE AS WINEEEE YALL! FIRE. NO NOTES. We obvi had gobs leftover I even had some for breakfast yesterday heheh 

Anywho! I will definitely go back to Antique Bar & Bakery, the vibes inside were nice and cozy, perfect for winter! Our waiter was fine, we had to ask for silverware when our food came because we had no silverware or napkins. Tables are close together so you can definitely hear the convos happening on the sides of you. 

All in all great experience and will be back tootles!😽😽

Zahra’s Journey Home — Part 4 🤍

Just when we thought the hardest part was over, Zahra reminded us she’s a master escape artist.

After her spay, she Houdini’d her way out of a surgical onesie and went after her sutures — which sent us to urgent care and onto antibiotics. That was the moment we decided… Christmas came early.

A sweater over the onesie did what nothing else could. She accepted her fate. No escapes. No tricks.

This wasn’t a day or a week — this was the month we had to adapt.

And she did. 🤍

Part 5 is where everything opens up 🐾

The Hive — Hoboken, New Jersy

This place has a line down the block before the doors even open, and for good reason. Their cinnamon rolls are known to sell out within the hour, with a new flavor released every month alongside the classic. I grabbed both the regular cinnamon roll and the lemon sage cinnamon roll from a Bliss Skincare collaboration, and it immediately made sense why people plan their mornings around this spot.

These rolls are massive in the best way. One bite is enough to satisfy the craving, and having two to myself was ambitious in hindsight. Soft, gooey, perfectly spiced, and rich without being overwhelming. They’re the kind of pastry you keep picking at all day and somehow never get tired of. They’ve also done a collaboration with Reese Witherspoon’s wine company, Drop of Sunshine, which honestly tracks once you taste how thoughtful everything is.

The seasonal drink menu is just as fun. Over the summer, I got the raspberry lemonade matcha which was bright, refreshing, and perfect for a summer day, and the lemon flavored cold foam on top made it even better. One of my personal favorite pastry from here is the peanut butter s’mores bar. The texture is spot on with a chewy center and a firmer outside, and the flavor combo is dangerously good. It’s huge, easy to pick at all day, and something I crave often, even if I have to actively stop myself from going too often.

What’s better than 1 peppermint mocha cinnie? 2. ❤️❤️

this week’s matcha spotlight is from @hellofromthehive 🤩 this is my fave matcha spot in hoboken/jersey city (& deeming a fave is a big deal). great wfh space & vibes as well like literally look at my to go bag they decorated in slide #3… SO CUTE. my absolute fave drink is the lucky charms matcha 🍀🌈 but its only a seasonal drink (i cried when i found out) so this is my formal petition to have it as part of the menu. regular matcha is amazing but i’ll be focusing on this special for this review hehe

📍: the hive - hoboken + jersey city, nj
🍵: lucky charms matcha latte
📝: perfect amount of creaminess! you would expect it to be super sweet but its NOT AT ALL! was still able to taste the matcha with just hints of the cereal because of the infused cereal milk (amazing concept for adding sweeteners)
⭐️: 10/10
👍: would recommend and have been back!! came here with the girls & they loved it 💞 vibes matched the yap session

A new kinda crowd gathered outside our Hoboken shop and it had nothing to do with cinnies ❤️ We proudly watched our city dedicate the shop’s corner to The Truglio Family, who occupied our corner far longer than we have. They served the community as the neighborhood butcher, but were much, much more to anyone who knew them. Their legacy is clear, given how often we get asked if we knew that our shop was once a butcher’s, and we feel deeply responsible to continue the tradition of serving and providing friendship to anyone who walks through our doors. Congratulations on the incredible moment 🥹
